brief: Two-pager for the Ministry of Education of Kenya about Giga school connectivity. Giga has mapped 2.3 million schools in 54 countries. In Kenya, a multi-vendor procurement model cut monthly connectivity costs by around 60%, from US$110-120 to about US$45 per school, and more than 600 schools have been connected through it. EU funding of 9.8 million euro backs a roadmap to connect 1,000 schools. Kenya is one of four pilot locations for Connectivity Credits. Ask: co-fund the next 1,000 schools, adopt Giga Meter nationally, join the Africa pooled tender.

Make an advocacy two-pager on connecting health facilities. Facts: about 1 billion people are served by health facilities without reliable electricity; in sub-Saharan Africa only 28% of health facilities have reliable power; connected clinics can track immunisations in real time and flag zero-dose children; UNICEF Digital Inclusion maps health facilities on Giga Maps, advises on procurement and builds investment cases. In Rwanda, 500 health centres were mapped in 2025; in Ghana, a pilot connected 120 clinics with satellite links. Our model: map, procure, finance. Audience: Ministers of Health at the World Health Assembly.

Partnership brief for telecom operators joining the Connectivity Credits programme. Connectivity Credits reward internet service providers with tradeable digital credits for each school they connect and keep online. Pilots run in Kenya, Rwanda, Brazil and Kazakhstan. 1,200 schools are in the pilot pipeline; each credit is verified with Giga Meter real-time data. Active partners: GSMA, Ericsson. What we ask of operators: commit coverage for at least 100 schools per country, share network maps, report service quality monthly. Contact: Maria Lopez, Partnerships Lead, Digital Inclusion, mlopez@unicef.org.

Product brief for Giga Meter. Giga Meter is a free app that measures school internet speed and uptime in real time. It runs on Windows, Android and Chrome. 145,000 schools report data through it across 30 countries. Governments use it to check that providers deliver the speed they are paid for. Status: version 3 launched in March 2026, with offline caching and a new admin dashboard. Next: a public API for ministries in 2027 and AI-readiness metrics (latency, bandwidth for AI tools).

Crea un two-pager per il Ministero degli Esteri italiano sulla collaborazione con UNICEF Digital Inclusion. L'Italia ha finanziato 2 milioni di euro nel 2025 per connettere le scuole in Mozambico e Malawi. Risultati: 850 scuole mappate in Mozambico, 310 scuole connesse in Malawi, prezzi della connettività ridotti del 35% grazie a una gara congiunta. Prossimi passi: estendere il modello alla Tanzania, finanziare l'energia solare per 200 scuole, co-progettare un fondo per la connettività in Africa australe.

Two-pager explaining what UNICEF Digital Inclusion does for child protection systems: digital birth registration, case management for social workers, and safe online spaces for adolescents. Explain why connectivity matters for each, how we work with governments and partners, and what we need from donors: flexible funding, technical partnerships, and policy support.
